description:
Soft Lavender is a metallic mica powder pigment for epoxy resin. Added at different concentrations it gives a range of effects — rippled metallic colour in river tables, worktops, castings and coatings, or accents in geode pieces, acrylic pours, polymer clay and jewellery work.

The very fine particles mix into any viscous, transparent medium and can be applied to any surface. Non-toxic and gentle on skin, supplied in a resealable 50 g jar.

A metallic mica powder in the Jungle colourway, a green shade, made to tint epoxy resin. Stirred into clear resin at varying concentrations it builds rippled metallic effects — in river tables, worktops, castings, geode art and acrylic pours — and it works equally in polymer clay, jewellery and woodwork.

Particles are very fine, so the powder blends into any viscous, transparent medium and takes to any surface. Non-toxic and gentle on skin, packed in a resealable 50 g jar.

Sparkling Pearls is a mica pigment coated with titanium dioxide and iron oxide, which lends pearlescent, iridescent effects to epoxy pours and thin coatings. At tiny additions the resin stays translucent, tinted with a shimmer that moves in the light; at higher loadings it reads as a solid colour, close to metallic paint. Shades can be blended dry, or poured as separately tinted resins for layered effects.

For full opacity, allow 1 g of pigment per ounce of epoxy (25–50 g per gallon of peelable paint). It suits river tables, worktops, castings, acrylic pours, polymer clay and jewellery work alike. Non-toxic and gentle on skin, supplied in a resealable 56 g jar.

A glow-in-the-dark pigment in Hot Pink. Charged under UV light it gives a bright, long-lasting glow — a thicker layer, or simply more powder, extends both the brightness and the duration, while grinding the powder reduces its luminosity. The pigment is stable below 160 °C.

It works in epoxy resin and in water-based media such as acrylic paint, and suits nail art and slime. Non-radioactive, non-toxic and gentle on skin, supplied in a resealable 56 g jar.

Orange glow-in-the-dark pigment. A short charge under UV light sets off a bright glow that lasts; using more powder, or laying it on thicker, makes the glow brighter and longer. Do not grind the powder — it weakens the luminosity. Stable below 160 °C.

Add it to epoxy resin or to water-based media such as acrylic paint; it also suits nail art and slime. Non-radioactive, non-toxic and gentle on skin, in a resealable 56 g jar.

A highly concentrated pigment paste in White Snowflake, made for epoxy resin work — beach-themed pours in particular — and for building cell and lacing effects. The formula is heavily pigmented, so a very small amount brings resin to a solid, rich colour; its thick consistency mixes in well, disperses easily and holds excellent UV stability.

Use between 2 and 5% pigment as a guide, keeping paste below roughly 10% by volume of the combined resin and hardener. Supplied in a 56 g (2 oz) jar.

Jesmonite AC100 is a water-based acrylic polymer composite used across construction and art projects. It is easy to work with, dries quickly, and cures to a durable finish that resists water, UV light and extremes of temperature. An environmentally friendly material, it suits work where sustainability matters as much as strength.

An additive that extends the setting time of Jesmonite, giving more working time and finer control over the cure. Retarders are material-specific — this one is for cement-based Jesmonite AC730, with a separate version made for AC100 — so match the retarder to the material in hand.

Add it to the pre-weighed liquids to extend the pot life of the mix. Typical inclusion rates run between 2 g and 8 g per kilogram; a 2% addition sets in roughly 25–30 minutes, though temperature, humidity and mix size all shift the timing, so a small test in your own workspace is recommended.

A terracotta pigment for colouring Jesmonite AC100, AC200 and AC300, blendable with the other Jesmonite pigments to reach almost any shade. Add it to the Jesmonite liquids by weight before the base goes in, at a maximum of 2% of the total mix — 20 g per kilo gives a strong, saturated colour; reduce the rate for lighter tones. Scales reading in 1 g increments are recommended.

The pigment is not UV stable, so it is recommended for interior projects only. Colours develop deeper and stronger in AC100 than in AC300, owing to AC100's higher acrylic content, and the same 2% rate will pigment plaster. Jesmonite base is a natural material subject to minor variation — worth allowing for in very pale casts. Shelf life is 24 months.

A liquid additive for Jesmonite AC100 that extends the setting time of the mix, allowing more working time and greater control over the cure. It also reduces the exotherm generated as the material cures and can improve the final surface finish. Blend it into the liquid component at a typical rate of 2–8 g per kilogram of mix; set times shift with temperature and humidity, so a test in your own workspace is recommended.

Suited to sculpture, architectural features and large-scale castings. For AC100 only — not recommended for other Jesmonite composites.

A translucent blue pigment from the Haksons concentrated range. Semi-transparent by nature, it colours resin while letting light — and the layers beneath — show through, which is the basis of layered effects. The ground affects the outcome: over a white substrate the shade reads lighter and more muted than over a dark one.

The effects range from subtle, nuanced tints to bold, vibrant colour.

Haksons concentrated pigment in translucent red. Because the pigment is semi-transparent, light passes through the tinted resin and the layers beneath stay visible, which allows layered effects; the final shade shifts with the substrate, reading lighter and more muted over white grounds than over dark ones.

The result ranges from subtle, nuanced tints to bold, vibrant colour.
